jal-mahal-man-sagar-2019.jpg.why_this_image: Hero. Jal Mahal standing in Man Sagar: the lake the developer's account in the 2014 Supreme Court judgment dates to Man Singh of Amer, where the north of the walled city's storm water ran in 1895 and its sewage was turned in 1962. The credit names no year for the palace or the dam (both disputed).

imperial-gazetteer-1908-ramgarh.jpg.why_this_image: Chapter 4. The 1908 description of the new Ramgarh reservoir: an 80-foot dam, 'the most important irrigation work in the Jaipur State', six square miles, 3,000 million cubic feet, 'practically complete'. No openly licensed photograph of the Ramgarh dam wall was found.

ramgarh-lake-2014.jpg.why_this_image: Chapter 5. The only openly licensed Ramgarh photograph found. The file page says only 'Ramgarh Lake, Jaipur district, India 2014', so the caption quotes that and does not claim from the photograph that the bed is dry; 'still bone dry' is the Supreme Court's record of 9 Nov 2017. Drop it if the owner prefers no low-resolution plate.

No openly licensed photograph of the Amanishah or Dravyavati channel exists on Commons (searches 'Dravyavati', 'Dravyawati', 'Amanishah nala', 'Jaipur nallah': no hits), so the river half of the chapter has no plate.

File:Jaigarh Fort water supply.jpg.reason: Subject unverified. The walled reservoir is probably the Sagar between Amer and Jaigarh, but nothing on the page says so, and no source for Sagar was found. Dropped rather than captioned on a guess.
